text: Twelve-hour shift on the ward. Two admissions, one discharge, no lunch. Home, shower, bed.
Delivered 180 parcels today. App says I was 4 minutes over target. Docked again.
Customer called me useless in front of the whole queue because the card machine was down. I smiled. I wanted to scream.
Clocked in 7am, clocked out 3pm. Stocked aisles 4 to 9. Break at 11.
Manager Brenda put me on the till, the floor and the stockroom at the same time. I can't be in three places.
A patient's daughter came back to the ward with chocolates and a card that said 'you made his last days gentle'. I had to go and sit in the sluice room.
Taxi shift. Drunk passenger was sick in the back at 2am. Cleaning fee won't cover it. Done for the night.
Warehouse is quiet this week. Picked my orders, chatted to Darnell on break, home on time. Fine by me.
Passed my forklift licence. Small thing to some people. Big for me.
Night shift again. Driving home at dawn while everyone else drives to work. Strange lonely feeling.
Agency rang: they've got me a permanent contract from next month. Proper sick pay. Proper holidays.
Rota changed with a day's notice again. I had a dentist appointment and a kid to pick up. Nobody asks.
Stood on my feet for ten hours. My knees are forty years older than me.
Training the new girl, Priya. She picks things up fast. Reminds me of me at nineteen. Nice feeling, passing it on.
Thinking about whether I want to stack shelves for another twenty years. The answer is probably no. Then what?
Black Friday. Opening at 6am. Queue already round the block at 5. Every till, every aisle, every second.
Cleaned the offices on floors 3 to 6. Emptied bins, hoovered, mopped the kitchen.
Boss shouted at me for a mistake that was in the system before I touched it. I showed him the log. He walked off without a word.
Hoping the promotion to shift lead comes through. Interviewed today. Think it went alright.
Lunch break in the van, rain on the roof, a flask of soup. Ten minutes of peace in a mad day.
Coffee machine at the café broke at 7:30am rush. Forty people, no coffee. I've never been hated by so many strangers.
Pay rise. Twenty pence an hour. After four years. Thanks, I'll treasure it.
Brought in samosas for the whole shift for Eid. The night team cleared the lot by 3am. Lovely feeling.
Back aching from lifting patients all week. Two of us for every job and they've cut us to one.
Bus driving shift: route 42, eight loops, one lost umbrella handed in, no incidents.
So grateful for Marta covering my shift when my son was sick. I'll do her Saturday.
Lonely job, this. Driving all day, talking to satnav. The radio presenters feel like friends.
Trying to decide whether to do the nursing degree at 38. Scared I've left it too late. Writing it down to see how it looks.
Short-staffed again. Three call bells at once, a fall in bay four, and the doctor wanting obs done now. I didn't know which way to turn.
Got 'employee of the month'. A certificate and a £20 voucher. Rolled my eyes but secretly chuffed.
The security guard at the gate, Femi, always asks about my mum. Nobody else here knows I have one.
Head office announced store closures. Ours is on the list. Eleven years.
Two days off in a row for once. Did absolutely nothing and it was brilliant.
Thinking about how I used to love this job. Somewhere in the last two years it became just a job.
Finished my first full week as a carer on my own rounds. Twelve clients, everyone fed and safe. Not bad.
Payslip says I've done 58 hours this week. My body says I've done about 200.
New manager actually listens. Asked our opinion on the rota. Hope it lasts.
Racist comment from a customer. Manager told me to 'let it go, he's a regular'. I won't let it go.
Booked the holiday! Ten days off in August. First proper break in two years.
Ironing pile, school uniforms, 6am alarm, double shift. I'm running on empty.
Filled in the timesheet. 39 hours. Sent it to payroll.
Night shift is peaceful at 4am. The ward breathes. Just me, the monitors and a cup of tea.
Three of us left in one month. Everyone else is applying elsewhere. I don't know whether to jump.
Kitchen was chaos tonight. Fifty covers, two chefs, one fryer working. Head chef threw a pan.
Reached my sales target for the first time. Ate cake in the stockroom. Small celebration.
Hoping the union gets us the back pay. Meeting next week. Fingers crossed.
Retirement party for Harold, forty years on the line. He cried. We all cried. Proud to have worked with him.
The client complained about the haircut I did exactly as she asked. Showed her the photo she brought. She left without paying.
Took the long way home past the river after the shift. Just needed the quiet. Felt better after.
Everyone at work went to the pub without me. Guess I'm not part of that group.
Got the job at the vet clinic! Start in two weeks. Can't stop telling people.
Standard shift. Unloaded two lorries, scanned the pallets, signed off at four.
I'm the only woman on this site. They're mostly fine, but some days I feel very alone in that portacabin.
Finally learned all the cocktail recipes. Made a perfect espresso martini without looking it up.
Feeling settled at the new job. Good team, fair boss, decent canteen. That's all I wanted.
Sick pay denied because I was off 'without enough notice'. I had a fever of 39.
So tired I fell asleep on the bus and woke up at the depot. Driver laughed. I didn't.
Lockers, mop buckets, the smell of bleach. Another night. Nothing to say really.
Excited for the conference in Manchester next week. First time the company has sent me anywhere.
Hope I can move to days soon. Doctor says the nights are hurting my sleep long-term.
Overwhelmed by the new system. Every order screen moved, every code changed, and the queue doesn't wait.
Calm day on the farm. Fed the animals, mended the fence, ate lunch on a hay bale.
Grateful for the regulars who tip in cash and ask after my kids. They make the job bearable.
Angry at myself for not speaking up when Kev took credit for the fix. Again.
Thinking about Dad, who did this same job at this same factory for thirty years. I get him more now.
Shift was sad. One of our long-term residents, Mr. Owusu, passed this afternoon. We all stood round his bed for a minute.
Contract renewal meeting Friday. If they don't renew, I'm out of work by Christmas.
Did the inventory, did the banking, locked up. Long but steady.
Exhausted after doubling up for Shona. She owes me three shifts now and counting.
Tidy, simple shift. Worked, chatted, home. That's a good day in this job.
